senses.gloss: (b. h.) to lie with, copulate with, cover.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 1:6:6">Y. Ab. Zar. I, 40ᵃ</cite> top <he>והלא מביא … והוא רוֹבְעָהּ וכ׳</he> but may he not bring (the crippled sire) to her, and he cover her, and she may give birth? <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 1:6:6">Ib.</cite> <he>והיא רוֹבַעַת ממנו וכ׳</he> and she (the crippled mare) may be fecundated by him.—Esp.

senses.gloss: (with ref. to Lev. XX, 16) to have connection with a beast.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 1:4">Snh. I, 4</cite> <he>הרוֹבֵעַ והנִרְבָּע</he> the animal that covered (a woman), and the animal that was covered (by a man).
senses.label: a

units: Snh. 9ᵇ פלוני רְבָעוֹ לאונסו וכ׳ (if a man says) such and such a man committed sodomy with him (euphem. for me) against his will, he himself in connection with another witness can testify &c.—Trnsf. to fructify the ground.
senses.label: b

senses.gloss: to be covered, esp. to be copulated in an unnatural way.
units: <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 24a:7">Ab. Zar. 24ᵃ</cite> <he>וולד הנִרְבַּעַת אסורה</he> the issue of a beast that was used for buggery while pregnant is disqualified for the altar; <he>היא וולדה נִירְבְּעוּ</he> for mother and child have been abused; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (v. רְבִיעָה) to inundate for the sake of improving the soil. Y. Peah VII, 20ᵇ (ref. to המרבץ, ib. V, 19ᵃ top) מביון שהוא מְרַבְּעָהּ וכ׳ because he inundates it, it will yield so much more next year.

units: <cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 306:22">Sifré Deut. 306</cite> <he>הוי מפטם … ומְרַבֵּע</he> perfume (thyself) with the words of the Law, and do it a second, a third, and a fourth time; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 942:2">Yalk. ib. 942</cite>.—
senses.label: a

senses.gloss: to quadrate, make quadrilateral. Part. pass. מְרוּבָּע; f. מְרוּבַּעַת; pl. מְרוּבָּעִים, מְרוּבָּעִין; מְרוּבָּעוֹת. Y. Maasr. V, end, 52ᵃ אין מר׳ מששת ימי בראשית there is no quadrangular form in natural objects; ib. והתנינן … הקילקי המ׳ but do we not read in the Mishnah (Neg. VI, 1) … ‘of the size of a Cilician bean which is quadrilateral’? כל גרמא … (ד)יְרַבְּעֶנָּהּ הוא this very passage proves that there is nothing quadrangular in nature; and why does the Mishnah say so? It means that he (the priest) should calculate the size of a bean by circumscribing a quadrilateral around it; Y. Ned. III, 37ᵈ bot.; Y. Shebu. III, 34ᵈ די ירבעונה הוא (read: יְרַבְּעֶינָּהּ).
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Ma'asrot 3:14">Tosef. Maasr. III, 14</cite>, v. <cite ref="C01336"><he>גָּרִיס</he></cite>. Y. Erub. II, 20ᵃ <he>מר׳</he> a quadrilateral stone, opp. <cite ref="P00083"><he>עגולה</he></cite>; Bab.
<cite ref="Eruvin 19b:21">Erub. 19ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Eiruvin 2:4">Tosef. ib. II</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Eiruvin 1:1">I</cite>), 1.

<cite ref="Tosefta Eiruvin 6:19">Ib. VI</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Eiruvin 5:10">V</cite>), 10 <he>ריבע את העיר וכ׳</he> if he squares a town (which is built in a curve) and makes the calculation as if it were a square table (plane); <cite ref="Eruvin 56b:1">Erub. 56ᵇ</cite> <he>המְרַבֵּעַ וכ׳</he>.
<cite ref="Eruvin 56b:1">Ib.</cite> <he>וחוזר ומרבע את התחומין</he> and then again he draws a square for the Sabbath limits.
<cite ref="Eruvin 56b:1">Ib.</cite> <he>כמה מר׳ יתר וכ׳</he> how much larger is the square than the inscribed circle?; a. fr.
